baby-yoga.desc: Gentle stretching, movement and songs for babies with a parent or carer. A calm first step into the studio.
tags: Come with a parent or carer
baby-yoga.who:
Babies from birth until they are confidently walking, with a parent, grandparent or carer on the mat beside them. It is as much for the grown-up as the baby: an hour of calm, songs and other adults to talk to.

No experience of yoga is needed, and everything is guided step by step. Starting this September.

steps.title: Settling in
steps.text: Mats out, shoes off and a hello song while everyone arrives and gets comfortable.

steps.title: Gentle stretches
steps.text: Guided stretches and movements for your baby, always at their pace, never forced.

steps.title: Songs and play
steps.text: Action songs, tickles and tummy time that build strength and bonding.

steps.title: Wind-down
steps.text: A calm finish so everyone leaves more relaxed than they arrived.

baby-yoga.lead: A natural next step into Parent & Toddler once they are on their feet.

wear.note: There is nothing to buy and no uniform. Come as you are.

parent-toddler.desc: Songs, props and simple movement with a grown-up alongside. Usually the first taste of class children get.
tags: Come with a parent or carer
parent-toddler.who:
Toddlers up to 2 and a half year with a parent, grandparent or carer joining in alongside them. For most families it is their first taste of a class, so it is built around play rather than performance.

Some children join in from the first song; others watch from a lap for a few weeks. Both are completely normal.

steps.title: A hello song
steps.text: The same song every week, so even the youngest know the class has started.

steps.title: Action songs and rhymes
steps.text: Marching, clapping and simple movement that builds rhythm and listening.

steps.title: Props out
steps.text: Scarves, pom-poms and shakers. This is most children's favourite part.

steps.title: A goodbye song and a sticker
steps.text: A calm finish and a sticker on the way out. The sticker matters.

parent-toddler.lead: Most children move up to First Steps when they are ready to try a class on their own.

wear.note: No uniform at this age. Come as you are.

first-steps.desc: The first class children take on their own. Rhythm, listening, balance and a lot of pretending to be animals.
first-steps.who:
Children aged 2 to 4 taking their very first class on their own. The class is small, the room is friendly and the teacher's job in the first weeks is simply to make it somewhere they want to come back to.

No experience is expected.

steps.title: A warm-up song they know
steps.text: Familiar songs to shake off the shyness and get bodies moving.

steps.title: Rhythm and listening games
steps.text: Clapping, stopping, starting and counting, disguised as games.

steps.title: Balance, jumps and simple steps
steps.text: First real dance steps, one at a time, with lots of repetition.

steps.title: A story dance to finish
steps.text: A short dance that tells a story, with a lot of creative exercises.

first-steps.lead: Second Steps when they start reception age.

wear.note: No uniform is needed for the first class. Anything they can move in is fine.

second-steps.desc: The bridge between play and technique. Children start learning proper positions and their first real routines.
second-steps.who:
Children from reception and including school year 1. It is the bridge between play and understanding and applying dance technique.

Children still play, but they also start to learn real positions, real names for steps and their first short routines.

steps.title: Warm-up and stretch
steps.text: A proper warm-up, taught as a routine they will come to know by heart.

steps.title: First positions
steps.text: Real technique in small doses: positions, posture and pointed toes.

steps.title: A routine to music
steps.text: A short dance built up week by week.

steps.title: A performance to finish
steps.text: A small show and tell for the parents to see what was learn during the lesson time.

second-steps.lead: Ballet, Tap or Jazz & Commercial, and a first medal for those who want one.

items: Anything they can move in (no denim, skirts or tights)
wear.note: No uniform is needed for the first class. Anything they can move in is fine.

ballet.desc: Graded technique, posture and musicality. It is the foundation under every other style we teach, and it shows.
ballet.who:
Children aged 4 and over. Ballet is the foundation we recommend under every other style: it builds the posture, strength and musicality that every other class draws on.

Classes are graded, so children work with others at their level and progress at a pace that suits them.

steps.title: Barre work
steps.text: Warm-up and technique at the barre, building strength and placement.

steps.title: Centre work
steps.text: Positions, port de bras and centre practise away from the barre.

steps.title: Travelling steps
steps.text: Steps and turns across the floor, broken down and repeated until they land.

steps.title: A short dance
steps.text: Putting the technique into a real piece of choreography to finish.

ballet.lead: Graded examinations and medals through our awarding bodies, and a place in the Christmas show. For older students, ballet underpins vocational applications.

items: Leotard and ballet skirt or shorts
Hair tied back, in a bun for exams
wear.note: No uniform is needed for the first class. Anything they can move in is fine.

jazz-commercial.desc: High-energy choreography, musicality and stage presence, in a class where individuality is encouraged rather than smoothed out.
jazz-commercial.who:
Anyone from four upwards who wants to move to music they recognise. Younger children work on coordination, counting and confidence in front of a room. Older students go further into technique, control and the kind of performance quality that reads from the back of a theatre.

You do not need any previous training. Roughly half the students in a beginner class have never danced before, and the class is taught with that in mind.

steps.title: Warm-up and conditioning
steps.text: Ten minutes of mobility and strength work so bodies are ready and injuries stay rare.

steps.title: Technique across the floor
steps.text: Turns, jumps, isolations and travelling steps, broken down and repeated until they land.

steps.title: Routine of the term
steps.text: A piece built up week by week, often the one they will perform at the Christmas show.

steps.title: Performance practice
steps.text: Running it full out, in groups, in front of each other. This is where the nerves go.

jazz-commercial.lead: Students who want to be assessed can take graded examinations and medals through our awarding bodies. Some students are invited into one of the three performing troupes. Everyone, whatever their level, gets a place in the annual show.

items: Leggings or shorts and a fitted top
A water bottle with their name on it
wear.note: No uniform is needed for the first class. Anything they can move in is fine.

tap.desc: Rhythm, timing and a lot of noise. One of the quickest routes to a first medal or graded examination.
tap.who:
Children aged 4 and over. Tap suits children who love rhythm and noise, and it gives quick wins: most students can make a real sound pattern in their first class.

No experience is needed, and it pairs well with Ballet or Jazz & Commercial.

steps.title: Warming up the feet
steps.text: Basic sounds and ankle work to switch the feet on.

steps.title: New sounds and steps
steps.text: One new step at a time, slowly, then up to speed.

steps.title: Combinations across the floor
steps.text: Joining steps into travelling patterns and rhythms.

steps.title: A routine everyone knows
steps.text: A class favourite to finish loud and together.

tap.lead: One of the quickest routes to a first medal or graded examination, and a place in the show.

items: Comfortable clothes they can move in
Tap shoes once settled; trainers to start
wear.note: No uniform is needed for the first class. Anything they can move in is fine.

acro-cheer.desc: Strength, flexibility and tumbling taught in a safe progression. Nobody is pushed past what their body is ready for.
acro-cheer.who:
Children aged 4 and over who love being upside down. Acro builds strength and flexibility; cheer adds lifts, balances and teamwork.

Everything is taught in a safe progression on mats, and nobody is pushed past what their body is ready for.

steps.title: A thorough warm-up
steps.text: Strength and flexibility work that makes the rest of the class safe.

steps.title: Skill progressions
steps.text: Rolls, cartwheels and walkovers, each broken into safe stages on mats.

steps.title: Group balances
steps.text: Partner and group work, building trust as much as technique.

steps.title: Putting it together
steps.text: Skills joined into short sequences and cheer routines.

acro-cheer.lead: Badges and awards as skills are signed off, and some of the most spectacular moments in the show.

items: Leggings or shorts and a fitted top
Hair tied back off the face
wear.note: No jewellery, for safety. No uniform is needed for the first class.

musical-theatre.desc: Born To Be is a musical theatre company that provides quality training in all things musical theatre; dance, singing and acting, through training, shows and performances.
musical-theatre.who:
Guarantee to provide all kinds of exciting opportunities for all students to perform on stage in yearly shows and concerts, make long lasting memories and to be apart of a loving community to explore, be themselves and have fun. With workshops, trips and weekly classes we hope for all students to find joy in musical theatre, whether that be onstage or off stage with opportunities to learn about all backstage jobs including costumes, sound and lighting and stage hands. 

Musical theatre is not just about performing, it’s about working as a team, creating characters, script work and so much more and we aim to cover all areas in an engaging and exciting way.

steps.title: Vocal and physical warm-up
steps.text: Voices and bodies switched on together.

steps.title: A number from a show
steps.text: Learning the song: melody, harmonies and words.

steps.title: Staging and character
steps.text: Who you are, where you stand and what the number is about.

steps.title: Run it like a performance
steps.text: Full out, with entrances and exits, as if the audience were in.

musical-theatre.lead: Featured roles in the Christmas show, and LAMDA work for students who want a qualification to aim at.

items: Comfortable clothes they can move and sing in
wear.note: No uniform is needed for the first class. Anything they can move in is fine.

drama.desc: One-to-one lessons in speech, monologue and audition work, including LAMDA examinations for students who want them.
drama.who:
Students aged 6 and over who want one-to-one coaching in speech, monologue and audition work. Some come for confidence, some for LAMDA examinations, some for both.

Lessons are private, so the pace and the material are chosen around one student.

steps.title: Voice and diction warm-up
steps.text: Breath, articulation and projection exercises.

steps.title: The current piece
steps.text: Detailed work on a monologue, poem or scene.

steps.title: Perform and refine
steps.text: Perform it through, then polish with honest, kind feedback.

steps.title: Practice for the week
steps.text: Clear, small things to work on before the next lesson.

drama.lead: LAMDA examinations, festival entries and audition preparation.

wear.note: Just bring the current piece and a water bottle.

singing.desc: Private lessons building range, breath and repertoire, working towards performances and graded examinations.
singing.who:
Singers of any age, from a first lesson to exam and audition preparation. Lessons are one-to-one, so the songs and the pace are chosen around the student.

Beginners are welcome; so are experienced singers who want to fix a specific habit or prepare for something particular.

steps.title: Breathing and warm-up
steps.text: Breath support and gentle vocal exercises to start.

steps.title: Technique
steps.text: Range, tone and control, worked through the current song.

steps.title: Sing it through
steps.text: Perform the song with coaching, section by section.

steps.title: What to practise
steps.text: A clear plan for the week, kept realistic.

singing.lead: Graded examinations, show solos and audition preparation.

wear.note: Bring water and, if you have one, the song you would love to sing.

troupes.desc: Notorious and Shockwave rehearse for professional performances and external events. Places are offered by invitation.
troupes.who:
Dedicated students aged 8 and over who are invited to join Notorious or Shockwave. Troupes rehearse to a professional standard and represent the school at external events.

Places are offered by invitation from class teachers, based on commitment as much as ability.

steps.title: Professional warm-up
steps.text: A disciplined warm-up, the same standard we would expect at a booking.

steps.title: Drilling the routines
steps.text: Current pieces run and corrected in detail.

steps.title: Formations and timing
steps.text: Cleaning: spacing, lines and synchronisation.

steps.title: Full run-throughs
steps.text: Complete runs with notes, performance-ready.

troupes.lead: Professional bookings and public events. Past bookings have included Alton Towers Scarefest.

items: Team kit, confirmed when a place is offered
Clean trainers kept for indoor use
Hair as agreed for the current pieces

ballroom-latin.desc: Waltz, quickstep, cha cha,  jive and more, taught by SJ. Come as a pair or on your own; we will partner you up.
ballroom-latin.who:
Adults who want to learn to dance properly, from complete beginners to returners. Waltz, quickstep, cha cha and jive, taught by SJ.

Come as a pair or on your own; we will partner you up. Absolute beginners are the norm, not the exception.

steps.title: Warm-up and posture
steps.text: Standing well is half of ballroom. We start there.

steps.title: A figure in the current style
steps.text: One new figure, broken down without a partner first.

steps.title: Dance it with a partner
steps.text: Putting the figure together, swapping partners if you wish.

steps.title: Put it to music
steps.text: Dancing the full sequence to music to finish.

ballroom-latin.lead: Medal tests for those who want them, and social dancing you can actually use.

items: Comfortable clothes you can move in
wear.note: Dance shoes can come later, once you are hooked.

adult-ballet.desc: For people who danced as a child and stopped, and for people who never got the chance. No leotard required.
adult-ballet.who:
Adults who danced as a child and stopped, and adults who never got the chance. The class is unhurried, sociable and taught without judgement.

No leotard required, no audience, and nobody is made to feel behind.

steps.title: A gentle barre
steps.text: Classic barre work at an adult-friendly pace.

steps.title: Technique at your pace
steps.text: Positions and placement, revisited properly.

steps.title: Centre and travelling
steps.text: Short combinations away from the barre.

steps.title: Stretch and unwind
steps.text: A proper stretch to finish. Most people's favourite part.

adult-ballet.lead: Entirely optional exams for those who want a goal, and the annual show for those who fancy it.

items: Anything comfortable you can move in
Socks, bare feet or ballet shoes

wedding-dance.desc: Your first dance, choreographed for you and taught privately at your pace. No experience needed.
wedding-dance.who:
Couples preparing for their first dance. Whether you want a gentle sway with confidence or full choreography, lessons are private and built around your song.

No experience needed. Best booked a few months ahead of the wedding, so nothing is rushed.

steps.title: Your song and ideas
steps.text: A chat about the song, the venue, the outfits and what you want it to feel like.

steps.title: The basic hold and steps
steps.text: Simple foundations you can rely on under pressure.

steps.title: Build the routine
steps.text: Your dance built section by section, at your pace.

steps.title: Polish until it feels easy
steps.text: Repetition until nerves have nothing to grab onto.

items: Shoes similar to your wedding shoes for later lessons
wear.note: Bring your song, even if you have three candidates.

custom-1786292058413.name: Adult Jazz Class
custom-1786292058413.desc: For people who danced as a child and stopped, and for people who have never got the chance.
custom-1786292058413.who:
Adults who have danced as a child and stopped, and adults who never got the chance. The class is sociable, full of fun and taught without judgement. 

No leotard required, no audience, and nobody is made to feel left behind.

steps.title: Warm - up
steps.text: Gentle stretch & flexibility

steps.title: Short Cardio
steps.text: A short cardio sequence taught in the form of a routine

steps.title: Teach Routine
steps.text: Each week a new routine gets taught with different levels of ability.

steps.title: Cool Down
steps.text: A nice relaxing stretch to end the class.
